facts.text: TV Camera was deployed at Sea of Tranquility during Apollo 11 in 1969.
The Westinghouse black-and-white TV camera that broadcast the first moonwalk to 600 million viewers. Armstrong set it on a tripod to film the EVA.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Transmitted the first live television broadcast from another world, enabling 600 million people to witness the moonwalk in real time and document the EVA procedures.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Sea of Tranquility.
Remains at Tranquility Base on its tripod; the original slow-scan video tapes were accidentally overwritten at NASA, but restored copies survive from broadcast recordings.
